details:
Basically, when I receive a notification it is most of the time from a new post from a group that I am in.

Then I click the Checkmark on the far left in the list of buttons to dismiss it.

And then sometimes a friend of mine sends an invite to their world and i do not want to join them right now as im busy talking to someone.

So out of muscle memory I click on the checkmark on the far left in the list of buttons, thinking that would dismiss the request. (well actually more like 'automated thinking')

HOWEVER, that instead accepts the request and puts me in their world, which I wasn't planning to do.

Of course you're supposed to click the X to deny the request, and that does make sense.

But like everywhere I go, even on this feedback website, the cancel/dismiss button is the LEFT button and the accept/submit button is the right button.

In my opinion I would consider this bad UX design. It makes me have to think before I click a button, which is not what you should want.

Of course there's probably a lot of people that are already used to the way it is right now, so I'm unsure if this should get changed.

However, maybe make the dismiss/deny button red or something? that would be a less 'radical' change, but would probably be more than enough for my brain to see: oh hey its red, that's probably the cancel/deny button!

Cause right now only the icon is different and on first glance you wouldnt even be able to see a difference between them, untill you look at it longer.
title: Bad UX design in notification dismiss
